summary: Splendor is a fast, tactile engine-building game where you spend chips to buy gem cards that discount future purchases, snowballing toward 15 points. Turns are simple and quick, but there's real tension in reading opponents' likely purchases and timing your reserves to deny key cards.
praised: Extremely easy to teach and learn, great gateway game
Satisfying tactile chip-collecting and engine-building feel
Nice production values (chunky chips, nice cards)
Scales well and plays fast at any player count
criticised: Can feel solitaire-ish with limited direct interaction beyond card/chip denial
Multiplayer solitaire feeling increases at higher player counts
Little variability between plays, can feel repetitive over many sessions
Card draw luck (which cards flip up) can swing a game
Fairly light strategically, not much long-term depth for hardcore gamers

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial via card reservation and chip scarcity

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: The winner is whoever first assembles the most efficient chain of discount cards to afford high-value cards and hit 15 points fastest.
